1	"""Core service surface for StreamMill.
2	
3	The frozen baseline only reports process health; that surface stays
4	unchanged. On top of it this module now implements named event-time
5	tumbling windows with explicit watermarks:
6	
7	* streams are created with a positive ``window_ms`` and a non-negative
8	  ``allowed_lateness_ms``;
9	* events carry an integer ``timestamp_ms`` and a finite numeric ``value``
10	  and land in the left-closed, right-open window
11	  ``[floor(timestamp_ms / window_ms) * window_ms, +window_ms)``;
12	* a per-stream watermark only moves forward; once it reaches
13	  ``window_end_ms + allowed_lateness_ms`` the window is final, is
14	  emitted exactly once, and is retained for queries;
15	* events with ``timestamp_ms < watermark - allowed_lateness_ms`` are
16	  acknowledged but dropped without touching the aggregates.
17	
18	Streams may optionally be created with a positive ``slide_ms`` (no
19	larger than ``window_ms`` and dividing it evenly). Such streams use
20	fixed-step overlapping sliding windows: an accepted event at timestamp
21	``t`` is counted once in every window ``[start, start + window_ms)``
22	whose ``start`` is an integer multiple of ``slide_ms`` and satisfies
23	``start <= t < start + window_ms`` (negative timestamps follow the same
24	mathematical grid). Every window still finalizes independently once the
25	watermark reaches its own ``window_end_ms + allowed_lateness_ms`` and is
26	emitted exactly once, ordered by window start. Without ``slide_ms`` the
27	stream is the plain tumbling stream above and every public shape is
28	unchanged.
29	
30	Streams may optionally enable event-id deduplication by passing a
31	positive ``dedup_retention_ms`` (no smaller than ``allowed_lateness_ms``)
32	at creation time. On such streams every event must carry a non-empty
33	string ``event_id``:
34	
35	* the first occurrence of an id is aggregated and remembered together
36	  with its ``timestamp_ms`` and ``value``;
37	* an exact retry (same ``timestamp_ms`` and numerically equal ``value``)
38	  is reported as ``duplicate: true`` and never touches the aggregates —
39	  the dedup check runs before the lateness check, so retained retries
40	  are duplicates even past the lateness horizon;
41	* the same id with a different timestamp or value is rejected with
42	  ``event_id_conflict`` and leaves all state untouched;
43	* an unseen id that arrives too late is dropped as usual and its id is
44	  not remembered.
45	
46	Remembered ids are evicted once the watermark advances past
47	``timestamp_ms + dedup_retention_ms`` (ids exactly on the boundary are
48	kept); evicted ids may be reused and are treated as new events.
49	
50	Streams created with a non-negative ``auto_watermark_lag_ms`` track the
51	maximum ``timestamp_ms`` of every successfully accepted event. After an
52	event is aggregated (and its id registered, when deduplicating) the
53	watermark advances atomically to
54	``max(current_watermark, max_event_timestamp - auto_watermark_lag_ms)``;
55	the lateness/dedup decision for that event uses the watermark as it was
56	before the advance. Dropped, duplicate or conflicting events never move
57	the maximum event timestamp or the watermark. Manual watermark posts keep
58	working on automatic streams and subsequent automatic advances never
59	regress below a manual watermark. Event responses on automatic streams
60	additionally carry the post-processing ``watermark_ms`` (``null`` until a
61	watermark exists) and the windows finalized by that response.
62	
63	A portable full-state snapshot is available through
64	``Service.snapshot`` / ``Service.restore_snapshot``: export produces a
65	self-contained JSON document (``format_version`` 1) capturing config,
66	watermark, open windows, finalized results and retained dedup records;
67	automatic streams additionally carry ``auto_watermark_lag_ms`` and
68	``max_event_timestamp_ms``; sliding streams additionally carry
69	``slide_ms`` (a document without it restores as a tumbling stream).
70	Restore is only accepted on an instance
71	without any streams, validates the document strictly (never silently
72	repairing it) and publishes the whole state atomically.
73	
74	In-process dimension tables provide the lookup side of an optional
75	current-value stream-table join:
76	
77	* ``POST /tables`` creates a named table; rows are written with
78	  ``PUT``-style upserts of non-empty string ``key``/``label`` pairs and
79	  report whether the stored label actually ``changed``;
80	* a stream may be created with ``lookup_table`` naming an existing
81	  table. Events on such a stream must carry a non-empty ``lookup_key``;
82	  after the usual dedup and lateness decisions the current label is read
83	  atomically (an unknown key is rejected with ``lookup_key_not_found``
84	  and leaves all state untouched) and the event is aggregated both into
85	  the plain windows and into per-window ``(lookup_key, label)`` groups.
86	  Later table writes only affect later events. Dedup records on joined
87	  streams include the ``lookup_key``, so resubmitting an id with a
88	  different key is an ``event_id_conflict``;
89	* joined groups finalize together with their window and are exposed
90	  through ``Service.joined_results``, ordered by window start, lookup
91	  key and label.
92	
93	Snapshots export as ``format_version`` 2 (adding ``tables`` plus
94	``lookup_table``/``joined_windows``/``joined_finalized`` on joined
95	streams) whenever any table exists, and restore stays compatible with
96	version 1 documents. When the join is unused every public shape and the
97	version 1 snapshot are unchanged.
98	
99	Streams may optionally materialize a window change feed by passing a
100	positive ``change_retention`` at creation time (echoed in the create
101	response; without it the stream behaves exactly as before). On such
102	streams every state change is published as a totally ordered sequence of
103	records, numbered by a ``seq`` that starts at 1 and never regresses:
104	
105	* every successfully aggregated event appends one ``upsert`` record per
106	  affected base window (ascending by window start on sliding streams),
107	  carrying the post-event ``count``/``sum`` of that window;
108	* every watermark advance that finalizes windows appends one ``final``
109	  record per newly finalized window (ascending by window start) with the
110	  final aggregates — on automatic streams the upserts of the triggering
111	  event always precede the finals of the resulting advance, and an
112	  advance without newly finalized windows appends nothing;
113	* duplicates, too-late drops, conflicts, unknown lookup keys and
114	  validation failures never consume a sequence number, and joined
115	  streams publish only the base-window changes.
116	
117	``Service.changes`` returns the retained records with ``seq`` greater
118	than a cursor, ascending, together with the current ``latest_seq``.
119	Only the newest ``change_retention`` records are kept (older ones are
120	trimmed after every commit, without moving ``latest_seq``); a cursor
121	past ``latest_seq`` raises ChangeCursorAheadError and a cursor that has
122	fallen behind the oldest retained record raises
123	ChangeCursorExpiredError.
124	
125	Instances with at least one change-feed stream export snapshots as
126	``format_version`` 3, which always carries the ``tables`` array and, on
127	enabled streams, ``change_retention``/``latest_seq``/``changes``.
128	Restore validates the retained records strictly (sequence continuity
129	against ``latest_seq`` and the retention cap, ordering, window
130	alignment, and the last retained record of every window against the
131	aggregated state) and publishes the feed so the cursor and the next
132	sequence number continue exactly as on the uninterrupted instance.
133	Version 1 and 2 documents restore as before, and instances without a
134	change feed keep exporting their original versions and shapes.
135	
136	Streams may optionally enable recoverable atomic batch ingestion by
137	passing a positive ``batch_retention`` at creation time (echoed in the
138	create response; without it the stream behaves exactly as before and the
139	batch entry point raises BatchIngestNotEnabledError). On such streams
140	``Service.add_batch`` accepts a non-empty ``batch_id`` plus 1 to 1000
141	events that each follow the stream's single-event rules:
142	
143	* the whole batch is applied at one consistent point, in input order and
144	  under the service lock, reusing the per-event dedup, lateness, lookup,
145	  window, automatic-watermark, finalization and change-feed semantics —
146	  no concurrent request can observe an intermediate state, and on
147	  automatic streams each element sees the watermark left by the
148	  previous one;
149	* the first event-id conflict or unknown lookup key aborts the batch and
150	  rolls back every state the earlier elements touched (aggregates, dedup
151	  records, watermark, finalized results, joined groups and change
152	  sequence), so a failed batch leaves the stream exactly as before and
153	  does not occupy its identifier; too-late drops and exact duplicates
154	  remain successful outcomes;
155	* a successful batch is remembered together with its request and full
156	  response. Within the retention a retry carrying the same field values
157	  in the same event order replays the stored response without writing
158	  again (and without refreshing the retention order), while the same
159	  ``batch_id`` with different content raises BatchIdConflictError. Only
160	  the newest ``batch_retention`` records are kept; evicted identifiers
161	  may be reused, and concurrent submissions of one identifier commit at
162	  most once.
163	
164	Instances with at least one batch-enabled stream export snapshots as
165	``format_version`` 4, which always carries the ``tables`` array and, on
166	enabled streams, ``batch_retention`` plus the retained batch records in
167	commit order. Restore validates the records strictly (identifier
168	uniqueness, the retention cap, and the request/response shapes against
169	the stream's features) and publishes them so replay and eviction behave
170	exactly as on the uninterrupted instance. Older document versions
171	restore as before.
172	
173	Dimension tables may optionally be declared event-time versioned by
174	passing ``event_time_versioned: true`` at creation time (echoed in the
175	create response; without it the table keeps the current-value overwrite
176	semantics above and every public shape is unchanged). A versioned table
177	receives rows of ``key``/``label``/``effective_from_ms`` through the
178	same row entry point: each version of a key is effective from its
179	``effective_from_ms`` until the key's next version, writes may arrive
180	out of order, a first write or a new effective time reports
181	``changed: true``, an identical retry reports ``changed: false``, and
182	an existing ``(key, effective_from_ms)`` point resubmitted with a
183	different label raises DimensionVersionConflictError and leaves the
184	history untouched. A stream whose ``lookup_table`` is versioned
185	resolves every event's label as the newest version with
186	``effective_from_ms <= timestamp_ms`` — late-arriving or backfilled
187	history therefore only affects events whose own event time it precedes
188	and never recomputes already received events; an unknown key or an
189	event time before the key's first version raises
190	LookupVersionNotFoundError with all state untouched. Dedup, lateness,
191	windowing, watermarks, change-feed sequence numbers and batch
192	atomicity (a missing version anywhere rolls the whole batch back) are
193	exactly as on current-value joins.
194	
195	Instances with at least one versioned table export snapshots as
196	``format_version`` 5, which always carries the ``tables`` array; each
197	table object records its mode, and versioned tables export their rows
198	as ``versions`` strictly ordered by ``key`` then ``effective_from_ms``.
199	Restore stays compatible with versions 1 to 4 and validates version 5
200	strictly (mode field combinations, duplicate or out-of-order versions,
201	invalid effective times and conflicting points all raise SnapshotError
202	without publishing partial state).
203	
204	Optional local persistence is available by pointing the
205	``STREAMMILL_STATE_FILE`` environment variable at a file path before
206	starting the HTTP server (``Service.from_state_file`` implements the
207	same startup contract in-process). Without the variable the service
208	keeps its pure in-memory behavior. With it, a missing file starts an
209	empty instance and an existing file is loaded as one snapshot document
210	under the exact restore contract above — invalid UTF-8, invalid JSON or
211	a document the restore entry point would reject (likewise an empty
212	path, a directory, or a missing/unwritable parent directory) aborts
213	startup before anything listens. Every successful state-changing
214	request (stream/table creation, row writes, events and batches,
215	watermark advances, snapshot restores) is then a single durable commit:
216	the complete post-commit snapshot is written atomically (temp file plus
217	rename, so the path only ever presents one complete snapshot) while
218	still holding the state lock, and only then is success returned.
219	Successful requests that leave the public state unchanged — too-late
220	drops, exact duplicates, identical row values, identical watermarks and
221	replays of retained batches — return their usual response without
222	touching the file, and failed requests never write either. If a persist
223	fails at runtime the in-memory state is rolled back to the pre-commit
224	snapshot, the file keeps the previous complete commit, and
225	StatePersistError is raised (HTTP 503 ``state_persist_failed``), so a
226	retry is processed exactly as if the request had never happened.
227	"""

336	def _write_state_file(path: str, document: dict) -> None:
337	    """Atomically replace the state file with one complete snapshot.
338	
339	    The document is serialized as UTF-8 JSON into a temporary file in
340	    the same directory, flushed and fsynced, then renamed over the
341	    target, so the configured path only ever presents the complete
342	    snapshot of one successful commit — a crash mid-write leaves the
343	    previous commit (or no file) intact. Any OS failure propagates as
344	    OSError with the target file untouched.
345	    """
346	    data = json.dumps(document, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")
347	    directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
348	    fd, temporary = tempfile.mkstemp(
349	        prefix=os.path.basename(path) + ".", suffix=".tmp", dir=directory
350	    )
351	    try:
352	        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
353	            handle.write(data)
354	            handle.flush()
355	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
356	        os.replace(temporary, path)
357	    except BaseException:
358	        try:

365	class _Table:
366	    """Mutable state of one dimension table. Guarded by the Service lock.
367	
368	    A current-value table keeps one label per key in ``rows``. An
369	    event-time versioned table instead keeps, per key, a timeline of
370	    ``(effective_from_ms, label)`` points strictly ascending by
371	    ``effective_from_ms``; a point is effective until the key's next
372	    point, and points may be inserted out of order.
373	    """
374	
375	    def __init__(self, event_time_versioned: bool = False) -> None:
376	        self.event_time_versioned = event_time_versioned
377	        # Current-value mode: key -> label.
378	        self.rows: dict[str, str] = {}
379	        # Versioned mode: key -> [(effective_from_ms, label), ...]
380	        self.versions: dict[str, list[tuple[int, str]]] = {}
381	
382	    def put_version(self, key: str, label: str, effective_from_ms: int) -> bool:
383	        """Insert one version point; return True when the history changed.
384	
385	        An identical retry of an existing point leaves the history
386	        untouched and reports no change; the same point with a different
387	        label is a conflict and also leaves the history untouched.
388	        """
389	        timeline = self.versions.setdefault(key, [])
390	        index = bisect.bisect_left(
391	            timeline, effective_from_ms, key=lambda point: point[0]
392	        )
393	        if index < len(timeline) and timeline[index][0] == effective_from_ms:
394	            if timeline[index][1] == label:
395	                return False
396	            raise DimensionVersionConflictError(
397	                f"version ({key!r}, {effective_from_ms}) already exists with a "
398	                f"different label"
399	            )
400	        timeline.insert(index, (effective_from_ms, label))
401	        return True
402	
403	    def label_at(self, key: str, timestamp_ms: int) -> str:
404	        """Newest label of ``key`` effective at ``timestamp_ms``.
405	
406	        Raises LookupVersionNotFoundError when the key is unknown or the
407	        timestamp precedes its first version.
408	        """
409	        timeline = self.versions.get(key)
410	        if not timeline:
411	            raise LookupVersionNotFoundError(key)
412	        index = (
413	            bisect.bisect_right(timeline, timestamp_ms, key=lambda point: point[0])
414	            - 1
415	        )
416	        if index < 0:
417	            raise LookupVersionNotFoundError(key)
418	        return timeline[index][1]

439	        self.dedup_retention_ms = dedup_retention_ms

443	        self.slide_ms = slide_ms

445	        self.lookup_table = lookup_table

454	        # maintained on automatic streams, None until the first such event.
455	        self.max_event_timestamp: int | None = None
456	        # window_start_ms -> [count, sum]; only non-empty windows exist.
457	        self._windows: dict[int, list] = {}
458	        self._finalized: list[dict] = []
459	        self._finalized_starts: set[int] = set()
460	        # event_id -> (timestamp_ms, value) for accepted, not yet evicted
461	        # ids; joined streams append the lookup_key to the tuple.
462	        self._dedup: dict[str, tuple] = {}
463	        # Joined streams only: window_start_ms -> (lookup_key, label) ->
464	        # [count, sum] for open windows, plus the finalized group rows in
465	        # results order (window start, lookup_key, label).
466	        self._joined_windows: dict[int, dict[tuple[str, str], list]] = {}
467	        self._joined_finalized: list[dict] = []
468	        # Change feed: the next record gets _latest_seq + 1; _changes
469	        # holds at most change_retention records, oldest first.
470	        self._latest_seq = 0

472	        # Retained batch records in commit order, at most batch_retention
473	        # of them; each is {"batch_id", "request", "response"}.
474	        self._batches: list[dict] = []

476	    @property
477	    def _step_ms(self) -> int:
478	        """Grid spacing: slide_ms for sliding streams, else window_ms."""
479	        return self.slide_ms if self.slide_ms is not None else self.window_ms

481	    def _window_starts(self, timestamp_ms: int) -> list[int]:
482	        """Starts of every grid window covering ``timestamp_ms``.
483	
484	        Windows are ``[start, start + window_ms)`` with ``start`` on the
485	        grid of multiples of the step; the floor division keeps the same
486	        boundaries for negative timestamps. The list is ascending, which
487	        is also the finalization/results order.
488	        """
489	        step = self._step_ms
490	        last = (timestamp_ms // step) * step
491	        first = last - (self.window_ms - step)
492	        return list(range(first, last + 1, step))

494	    def add_event(

509	        the resulting monotone watermark advance) only runs after
510	        aggregation and dedup registration.
511	
512	        On joined streams the label for ``lookup_key`` is read through
513	        ``label_of`` after the dedup and lateness decisions but before
514	        any state mutation, so an unknown key (or, on a versioned table,
515	        a timestamp before the key's first version) raises with all

518	        with a different key conflicts.
519	        """
520	        automatic = self.auto_watermark_lag_ms is not None
521	        joined = self.lookup_table is not None
522	        if self.dedup_retention_ms is not None:
523	            retained = self._dedup.get(event_id)
524	            if retained is not None:
525	                same = retained[0] == timestamp_ms and retained[1] == value
526	                if joined:
527	                    same = same and retained[2] == lookup_key
528	                if same:
529	                    outcome: dict = {"dropped": False, "duplicate": True}
530	                    if automatic:
531	                        outcome.update(watermark_ms=self.watermark, finalized=[])
532	                    return outcome
533	                raise EventIdConflictError(event_id)
534	            if self._is_too_late(timestamp_ms):
535	                # Unseen too-late ids are dropped without being remembered.
536	                outcome = {"dropped": True, "duplicate": False}
537	                if automatic:
538	                    outcome.update(watermark_ms=self.watermark, finalized=[])
539	                return outcome
540	            label = self._resolve_label(label_of, lookup_key, timestamp_ms)
541	            self._aggregate(timestamp_ms, value, lookup_key, label)
542	            self._dedup[event_id] = (
543	                (timestamp_ms, value, lookup_key)
544	                if joined
545	                else (timestamp_ms, value)
546	            )
547	            outcome = {"dropped": False, "duplicate": False}
548	        else:
549	            if self._is_too_late(timestamp_ms):
550	                outcome = {"dropped": True}
551	                if automatic:
552	                    outcome.update(watermark_ms=self.watermark, finalized=[])
553	                return outcome
554	            label = self._resolve_label(label_of, lookup_key, timestamp_ms)
555	            self._aggregate(timestamp_ms, value, lookup_key, label)
556	            outcome = {"dropped": False}
557	        if automatic:
558	            newly = self._note_accepted_event(timestamp_ms)
559	            outcome.update(watermark_ms=self.watermark, finalized=newly)
560	        return outcome

562	    def apply_batch(self, events: list[dict], label_of=None) -> list[dict]:
563	        """Apply a whole batch atomically, in input order.
564	
565	        Every element goes through the regular single-event path, so
566	        dedup, lateness, lookup, window, automatic-watermark,
567	        finalization and change-feed semantics are identical to posting
568	        the events one by one; each element observes the state left by
569	        the previous ones. The first EventIdConflictError or
570	        LookupKeyNotFoundError rolls every mutation back — aggregates,
571	        dedup records, watermark, finalized results, joined groups and
572	        the change sequence — so a failed batch leaves no trace.
573	        """
574	        backup = self._state_backup()
575	        outcomes: list[dict] = []
576	        try:
577	            for event in events:
578	                outcomes.append(
579	                    self.add_event(
580	                        event["timestamp_ms"],
581	                        event["value"],
582	                        event.get("event_id"),
583	                        event.get("lookup_key"),
584	                        label_of,
585	                    )
586	                )
587	        except Exception:
588	            self._state_restore(backup)
589	            raise
590	        return outcomes

592	    def _state_backup(self) -> tuple:
593	        """Deep snapshot of every mutable structure a batch can touch."""
594	        return (
595	            self.watermark,
596	            self.max_event_timestamp,
597	            copy.deepcopy(self._windows),
598	            copy.deepcopy(self._finalized),
599	            set(self._finalized_starts),
600	            copy.deepcopy(self._dedup),
601	            copy.deepcopy(self._joined_windows),
602	            copy.deepcopy(self._joined_finalized),
603	            self._latest_seq,
604	            copy.deepcopy(self._changes),
605	        )

607	    def _state_restore(self, backup: tuple) -> None:
608	        (
609	            self.watermark,
610	            self.max_event_timestamp,
611	            self._windows,
612	            self._finalized,
613	            self._finalized_starts,
614	            self._dedup,
615	            self._joined_windows,
616	            self._joined_finalized,
617	            self._latest_seq,
618	            self._changes,

621	    def _resolve_label(self, label_of, lookup_key: str | None, timestamp_ms: int):
622	        """Read the label for a joined event, or None on plain streams.
623	
624	        The reader receives the event's own ``timestamp_ms`` so a
625	        versioned table resolves the version effective at event time; a
626	        current-value table ignores it.
627	        """
628	        if self.lookup_table is None:
629	            return None
630	        return label_of(lookup_key, timestamp_ms)

632	    def _is_too_late(self, timestamp_ms: int) -> bool:
633	        return (
634	            self.watermark is not None
635	            and timestamp_ms < self.watermark - self.allowed_lateness_ms
636	        )

638	    def _note_accepted_event(self, timestamp_ms: int) -> list[dict]:
639	        """Advance the max event timestamp and then the watermark."""
640	        if (
641	            self.max_event_timestamp is None
642	            or timestamp_ms > self.max_event_timestamp
643	        ):
644	            self.max_event_timestamp = timestamp_ms
645	        target = self.max_event_timestamp - self.auto_watermark_lag_ms
646	        if self.watermark is None or target > self.watermark:
647	            # Publish through the shared path so finalization and dedup
648	            # eviction behave exactly like a manual advance.
649	            return self.advance_watermark(target)
650	        return []

652	    def _aggregate(
653	        self,
654	        timestamp_ms: int,
655	        value: float,
656	        lookup_key: str | None = None,
657	        label: str | None = None,
658	    ) -> None:
659	        for start in self._window_starts(timestamp_ms):
660	            bucket = self._windows.setdefault(start, [0, 0])
661	            bucket[0] += 1
662	            bucket[1] += value
663	            # Base-window upsert with the post-event aggregates; sliding
664	            # streams publish one record per window, ascending by start.
665	            self._append_change("upsert", start, bucket[0], bucket[1])
666	            if self.lookup_table is not None:
667	                groups = self._joined_windows.setdefault(start, {})
668	                group = groups.setdefault((lookup_key, label), [0, 0])
669	                group[0] += 1
670	                group[1] += value

672	    def _append_change(self, kind: str, start: int, count: int, total: float) -> None:
673	        """Publish one change-feed record and trim to the retention cap.
674	
675	        Sequence numbers are handed out consecutively from 1 and never
676	        regress; trimming only drops the oldest retained records.
677	        """
678	        if self.change_retention is None:
679	            return
680	        self._latest_seq += 1
681	        self._changes.append(
682	            {
683	                "seq": self._latest_seq,
684	                "kind": kind,
685	                "window_start_ms": start,
686	                "window_end_ms": start + self.window_ms,
687	                "count": count,
688	                "sum": total,
689	            }
690	        )
691	        overflow = len(self._changes) - self.change_retention
692	        if overflow > 0:
693	            del self._changes[:overflow]

695	    def advance_watermark(self, watermark_ms: int) -> list[dict]:
696	        if self.watermark is not None and watermark_ms < self.watermark:
697	            raise WatermarkRegressionError(
698	                f"watermark {watermark_ms} is below current {self.watermark}"
699	            )
700	        self.watermark = watermark_ms
701	        newly: list[dict] = []
702	        for start in sorted(self._windows):
703	            if start in self._finalized_starts:
704	                continue
705	            end = start + self.window_ms
706	            if watermark_ms >= end + self.allowed_lateness_ms:
707	                count, total = self._windows[start]
708	                newly.append(
709	                    {
710	                        "stream": self.name,
711	                        "window_start_ms": start,
712	                        "window_end_ms": end,
713	                        "count": count,
714	                        "sum": total,
715	                    }
716	                )
717	                self._finalized_starts.add(start)
718	                # The final record of a window always follows every
719	                # upsert of the triggering commit.
720	                self._append_change("final", start, count, total)
721	                if self.lookup_table is not None:
722	                    # Joined groups finalize synchronously with their window,
723	                    # ordered by (lookup_key, label) within it.
724	                    groups = self._joined_windows.pop(start, {})
725	                    for key, group_label in sorted(groups):
726	                        group_count, group_sum = groups[(key, group_label)]
727	                        self._joined_finalized.append(
728	                            {
729	                                "stream": self.name,
730	                                "window_start_ms": start,
731	                                "window_end_ms": end,
732	                                "lookup_key": key,
733	                                "label": group_label,
734	                                "count": group_count,
735	                                "sum": group_sum,
736	                            }
737	                        )
738	        self._finalized.extend(newly)
739	        if self.dedup_retention_ms is not None:
740	            horizon = watermark_ms - self.dedup_retention_ms
741	            self._dedup = {
742	                event_id: kept
743	                for event_id, kept in self._dedup.items()
744	                if kept[0] >= horizon
745	            }
746	        return newly

748	    def results(self) -> list[dict]:
749	        return [dict(row) for row in self._finalized]

751	    def to_snapshot(self) -> dict:
752	        """Serialize this stream as one entry of a version-1 snapshot."""
753	        entry: dict = {
754	            "name": self.name,
755	            "window_ms": self.window_ms,
756	            "allowed_lateness_ms": self.allowed_lateness_ms,
757	            "dedup_retention_ms": self.dedup_retention_ms,
758	            "watermark_ms": self.watermark,
759	            "windows": [
760	                {
761	                    "window_start_ms": start,
762	                    "window_end_ms": start + self.window_ms,
763	                    "count": self._windows[start][0],
764	                    "sum": self._windows[start][1],
765	                }
766	                for start in sorted(self._windows)
767	                if start not in self._finalized_starts
768	            ],
769	            "finalized": sorted(
770	                (dict(row) for row in self._finalized),
771	                key=lambda row: row["window_start_ms"],

775	            # Automatic streams publish the pair together; manual streams

777	            entry["auto_watermark_lag_ms"] = self.auto_watermark_lag_ms

779	        if self.slide_ms is not None:
780	            # Sliding streams publish the step; documents without it
781	            # restore as tumbling streams.
782	            entry["slide_ms"] = self.slide_ms
783	        if self.lookup_table is not None:
784	            # Joined streams publish the table reference plus the grouped
785	            # state; only format_version 2 documents may carry these.
786	            entry["lookup_table"] = self.lookup_table
787	            joined_open = []
788	            for start in sorted(self._joined_windows):
789	                groups = self._joined_windows[start]
790	                for key, group_label in sorted(groups):
791	                    group_count, group_sum = groups[(key, group_label)]
792	                    joined_open.append(
793	                        {
794	                            "window_start_ms": start,
795	                            "window_end_ms": start + self.window_ms,
796	                            "lookup_key": key,
797	                            "label": group_label,
798	                            "count": group_count,
799	                            "sum": group_sum,
800	                        }
801	                    )
802	            entry["joined_windows"] = joined_open
803	            entry["joined_finalized"] = [dict(row) for row in self._joined_finalized]
804	        if self.dedup_retention_ms is not None:
805	            records = []
806	            for event_id, kept in sorted(self._dedup.items()):
807	                record = {
808	                    "event_id": event_id,
809	                    "timestamp_ms": kept[0],
810	                    "value": kept[1],
811	                }
812	                if self.lookup_table is not None:
813	                    record["lookup_key"] = kept[2]
814	                records.append(record)

816	        if self.change_retention is not None:
817	            # Change-feed streams publish the config, the cursor and the
818	            # retained records; only format_version 3 documents may carry
819	            # these.
820	            entry["change_retention"] = self.change_retention
821	            entry["latest_seq"] = self._latest_seq
822	            entry["changes"] = [dict(record) for record in self._changes]
823	        if self.batch_retention is not None:
824	            # Batch-enabled streams publish the config plus the retained
825	            # batch records in commit order; only format_version 4
826	            # documents may carry these.
827	            entry["batch_retention"] = self.batch_retention
828	            entry["batches"] = copy.deepcopy(self._batches)
829	        return entry
